title: Monica's dream (3.11)
hookLine: she dreams she and her son stand on the same wooden rule
tomorrow: who was the friend he called half of his soul?

cards: A porch light left on all night for someone who isn't home yet. Augustine's mother, Monica, waited like that. And what did she see in her dream?
She was standing on a wooden rule, a long straight edge, grieving. A bright young man came toward her, cheerful, and asked why she was sad.

teach.h: WHERE YOU ARE, HE IS TOO.
teach.b: She told him she was mourning her son's ruin. He told her to look, and see that where she was, there her son was too. She looked, and there was Augustine, beside her on the same rule.
When she told him the dream, he tried a clever reading: maybe it meant she'd come over to where he was. She answered at once. No.
It wasn't said where he is, you are too. It was said where you are, he is too. Augustine writes that her quick answer moved him more than the dream itself.
Monica doesn't step off her rule to stand where her son is. She stays, and in the dream he's brought to her. And Augustine is honest that it didn't happen soon.
Years went by, he says, while he stayed in the mud and she kept praying.
So this whole week, the narrow room, the nursery, Dido, the pear tree, Carthage, the book on fire, was lived while someone stood on a rule, praying for him.

how: Catholic parents may ask Saint Monica's intercession for children who have drifted from the faith, and the Church keeps her memorial on the day before Augustine's.

o: a mother dreaming she'll follow her son abroad
a mother told her son will stand where she stands
a mother warned in a dream her son will die

p: where you are, he is too

s: in the dream, Monica is told she'll go where her son is
that was Augustine's clever reading. she answered no: where you are, he is too.
Augustine says her quick answer moved him more than the dream
he saw through his own trick because she did, without a pause.
Augustine came around soon after the dream
years went by, he says, while she kept praying.

games.q: your older brother left the faith and moved across the country. your mom wants to go to his city's parish to win him back. what does Monica's dream suggest?
o: stay where she stands, keep praying, and keep the door open.
move closer and argue him back before it's too late.
stop praying for him, since he chose to leave.
games.why: Monica doesn't step off her rule to stand where her son is. she stays, and in the dream he's brought to her. it took years.

practice: Send one short message to someone who feels far off, in faith, in hope or just in distance, a line that asks for nothing back. Then put the phone down and stay where you are with their name, the way Monica stayed on her rule.
Catholics who pray might ask God, quietly, to bring that person to stand beside them.

wordCard.voice: Monica's dream. A mother on a wooden rule, told that where she stands, her son will stand too.

orig.note: Latin, a straight edge or ruler; also a rule, a measure to live by.

carryVoice: Here's your line: the same rule, kept by someone who waited instead of chasing. A week of Augustine, done.
